result.title: Constructing physical mechanisms with artificial intelligence
result.summary: Mechanisms recur across the sciences: the equation for heat in a solid also describes molecular diffusion or a Brownian particle. A mechanism is rarely written in one equation; its operation, boundaries, parameters and closures are stated at different steps of a derivation, where methods that read text or fit formulas miss it. We built an equation-native system that reads the equations of all 2.5 million arXiv manuscripts, and show that mechanisms can be compiled from them and constructed by deterministic calculation. A constructor detaches, transfers, unfolds, composes and joins their parts across disciplines; where parts do not fit, the failure is an equation for the missing term. Constructions turn a threshold reactor into a memory that a weak signal writes, an oscillator into a switch through two changes that each fail alone, and a rhythm into the regulator of a chemical amount, each with conditions for an experimental test.

AI.brief_summary: 构建 equation-native 系统读取约 250 万篇 arXiv 论文中的方程，将散落在推导各步的机制信息编译出来，并用确定性计算跨学科地拆分、迁移、展开、组合机制部件，把「部件不匹配」的失败转化为缺失项的方程。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「拆解—迁移—重组」的机制构造与以失配定位缺失项的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的可组合结构、中间步骤贡献分配提供概念类比；但该工作不涉及视觉或多模态推理，线索需人工核查。
